stick_trigonometry_an_approximation_but_.question: Trigonometry - an approximation, but not complete
references: L. Euler, Introductio in analysin infinitorum (1748) (e^{i theta} = cos + i sin)
spherical trigonometry (Gauss-Bonnet; the angle sum exceeds pi by area/R^2)
stick_trigonometry_an_approximation_but_.statement: The trigonometric identities are exact, but trigonometry is an approximation and not complete in three precise senses: its function values are truncated infinite series; the real functions are projections of the complex exponential; and planar trigonometry is the flat-space limit of a curved geometry. The claim is TRUE within these senses and is not extended beyond them.

ticks.claim: [1 - computation is approximation] sin(theta) = theta - theta^3/6 + theta^5/120 - ... To two terms, sin(0.1) ~ 0.1 - 0.1^3/6 = 0.09983333 (sealed); the exact value differs at the next term (0.1^5/120 ~ 8.3e-8). Every finite computation of a trig function is a TRUNCATION of an infinite series - exact only in the limit. In that sense trigonometry is an approximation.

[2 - incomplete without i] cos^2(theta) + sin^2(theta) = 1: at theta=pi/6, (sqrt3/2)^2 + (1/2)^2 = 1.0 (sealed) - the unit circle. But cos and sin are only the REAL and imaginary projections of the complete object e^{i theta} = cos theta + i sin theta, a point on that circle in the COMPLEX plane (Euler). Real trigonometry alone is not complete; the whole requires the imaginary unit.

[3 - flat is an approximation to curved] Planar trigonometry assumes a triangle's angles sum to pi. On a sphere they do not: a triangle with three right angles sums to 3*(pi/2) = 3pi/2, exceeding pi by the spherical excess pi/2 = 1.570796 (sealed), which equals its area/R^2. Euclidean trig is the FLAT-space limit; under curvature (spherical, hyperbolic, and the curved spacetime of general relativity - ties stick_time_and_space_emergent_and_relational) it is incomplete.

[the discernment] The claim 'trigonometry is an approximation, but not complete' is TRUE in exactly three senses, all sealed above: truncated computation, projection of the complex exponential, and the flat limit of curved geometry. The engine affirms these and DELIMITS them - the pure identities themselves (cos^2+sin^2=1) are exact, not approximate. The shadow (real trig) points to the whole (the complex circle; curved geometry) - the same outline-of-what-it-lacks pattern as the Hole. Seal the arithmetic, affirm the true senses, claim nothing past them. Map, never launder.
